criteria.text: The participant has a pathologically (histologically or cytologically) proven diagnosis of non-operable stage IIB or III, node positive (American Joint Committee on Cancer [AJCC] eighth edition) non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with known PD-L1 status prior to registration
The participant has an identified primary tumor and at least one nodal metastasis (peribronchial/hilar/intrapulmonary, mediastinal/subcarinal, supraclavicular/scalene)
The participant has received up to 4 cycles of systemic therapy prior to registration for the current study cancer, and any prior chemotherapy for a different cancer is permissible
The participant refuses surgery, or is technically unresectable, or is medically inoperable
The participant has separate tumor nodules in the same lobe of the primary tumor
The participant is deemed clinically appropriate for curative intent definitive combined modality therapy
A history and physical examination is performed prior to registration
An MRI scan of the brain (preferred) or CT scan of the brain (if available, contrast is preferred for all neuroimaging) is performed prior to registration

A CT chest with IV contrast (if contrast is available and unless contraindicated, such as for abnormal kidney function) is performed prior to registration. PET/CT may be used if the CT portion is of identical diagnostic quality as achieved in a stand-alone CT
There is no evidence of distant metastases based on an FDG PET/CT scan obtained within 60 days of registration
The primary tumor is <= 7 cm
The participant is >= 18 years old
The participant has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0-2
Hematologic function (e.g. platelets, leukocytes, hemoglobin) is amenable, at the discretion of the treating physician, to allow for treatment with chemotherapy and concurrent radiation therapy
Creatinine clearance is >= 25 mL/min by the Cockcroft-Gault (C-G) equation
The participant has a non-malignant pleural effusion that is not known or demonstrated to be an exudative effusion
If a pleural effusion is present, criteria must be met to exclude malignant involvement
When pleural fluid is visible on both the CT scan and on a chest x-ray, a pleuracentesis is performed to confirm that the pleural fluid is cytologically negative
Effusions that are minimal (i.e., not visible on chest x-ray) that are too small to safely tap are eligible

The medical history is consistent with the patient being amenable, at the discretion of the treating physician, to allow for treating with consolidation immunotherapy. The participant has a known EGFR/ALK/other driver mutation at the time of registration, and can be treated with consolidation systemic therapy at the discretion of the treating physician
The participant has a prior or concurrent malignancy whose natural history or treatment does not have the potential to interfere with the safety or efficacy assessment of the investigational regimen
The participant has a negative pregnancy test <= 14 days prior to registration if of childbearing potential

The patient or a legally authorized representative provides study-specific informed consent prior to study entry and, for patients treated in the United States (U.S.), authorization permitting release of personal health information

The participant has had prior radiotherapy to the study cancer (local recurrence), or prior radiotherapy for a different cancer/condition to the region of the study cancer that would result in overlap of radiation therapy fields that is determined by the treating physician to impede the treatment of the study malignancy

The participant does not have an identifiable primary tumor and at least 1 pathologically enlarged lymph node (T3-4N0 or T0N1-3 patients are not eligible). At least 1 radiographically-involved lymph node is required, but pathologic confirmation of involvement is not mandated

The participant has a centrally located primary tumor < 2 cm from involved nodal disease that would result in significant overlap of the primary SBRT and nodal radiation fields. This does not include proximity to involved segmental and subsegmental lymph nodes (levels 13 and 14) that would not result in overlap of dose to the proximal bronchial tree or esophagus. Centrally located is defined as within or touching the zone of the proximal bronchial tree, which is a volume 2 cm in all directions around the proximal bronchial tree (carina, right and left main bronchi, right and left upper lobe bronchi, intermedius bronchus, right middle lobe bronchus, lingular bronchus right and left lower lobe bronchi)
The participant is pregnant or unwilling to discontinue nursing

The participant is of childbearing potential and is unwilling to use highly effective contraceptives during therapy and for the Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-labeled contraception timeframe required after the final dose of the selected systemic therapy regimen, because the treatment in this study may be significantly teratogenic
